issues.legal_issue: Related injured eyewitnesses may provide a sufficient basis for conviction when their presence and credible account are supported by their injuries, and immaterial discrepancies do not undermine that account.
material_facts: Several prosecution eyewitnesses were related to one another, but the principal witnesses had injuries consistent with their presence at the assault.
The Supreme Court found no cogent reason to disbelieve those witnesses and considered the discrepancy about people working in a nearby field immaterial.
The discrepancy about when police received information did not establish that the information was precise before the police officer arrived.

The accused's account that the complainant group attacked them was considered implausible because the complainant group had many injuries, including grievous injuries, while two accused had only a small number of visible injuries; the accused persons' injuries were explained as occurring while blows were warded off.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness evidence was reliable, and the discrepancies and accused persons' injuries did not justify rejecting the prosecution case; the conviction was supported by the evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The fact that eyewitnesses are related is not, by itself, a sufficient reason to discredit them. Their injuries may corroborate their presence, and discrepancies that are not material do not undermine otherwise credible testimony. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_from_acquittal_reversed and injured_witnesses_were_present and eyewitness_account_was_credible and discrepancies_were_immaterial

predicates.appeal_from_acquittal_reversed: The case is an appeal in which a higher court reversed an acquittal and entered a conviction.
predicates.injured_witnesses_were_present: Prosecution eyewitnesses sustained injuries consistent with their presence at the occurrence.
predicates.eyewitness_account_was_credible: The court found the eyewitness account credible and found no cogent reason to disbelieve it.
predicates.discrepancies_were_immaterial: The differences in the accounts did not materially undermine the witnesses' credibility or the prosecution case.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows reversal of an acquittal, injured witnesses were present, their account is credible, and discrepancies are immaterial, the conviction is supported by reliable evidence.

issues.legal_issue: Members of a group may be held liable for grievous injuries inflicted in pursuit of their common object even if the evidence does not establish which particular member caused each injury.
material_facts: The accused appellants attacked the complainant group together, carrying different weapons.
Several grievous injuries were inflicted, including injuries caused by sharp-pointed weapons.
The Supreme Court found that the circumstances showed the grievous injuries were inflicted in pursuit of the group's common object, even if one appellant did not personally cause an injury.
issues.conclusion: The uncertainty about which appellant inflicted particular injuries did not exculpate any appellant, because the grievous injuries were caused in prosecution of the group's common object.
issues.legal_principle: Section 326 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code imposes liability for grievous injuries caused in prosecution of an unlawful assembly's common object; individual proof that every member personally inflicted an injury is not required where the common object and the injuries' connection to it are established. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_after_acquittal_reversed and group_attack_occurred and common_object_to_cause_grievous_injuries and individual_injury_attribution_uncertain

predicates.appeal_after_acquittal_reversed: The case is an appeal following a higher court's reversal of an acquittal and entry of a conviction.
predicates.group_attack_occurred: Several people acting together attacked the victims.
predicates.common_object_to_cause_grievous_injuries: The circumstances showed that the group shared an object of causing grievous injuries.
predicates.individual_injury_attribution_uncertain: The evidence did not establish which particular group member caused every grievous injury.

issues.definition: When a group acts together with the common object of causing grievous injuries, uncertainty about which member inflicted each injury does not prevent liability for the injuries caused in pursuit of that object.
